question: The Indian High Courts Act was passed in the year ______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**1861**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Indian High Courts Act was passed in **1861** during British rule in India.
 
• This act paved the way for the establishment of **High Courts in major presidencies** such as Calcutta, Bombay, and Madras.
 
• It replaced the Supreme Courts and Sadar Adalats that were functioning in these presidencies at the time.
 
• The High Courts established under this act were vested with **civil, criminal, and appellate jurisdiction**.
 
• The Indian High Courts Act of 1861 is considered a significant step in the judicial reforms in colonial India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Supreme Courts and Sadar Adalats:**

 
 
• Before the High Courts were established, **Supreme Courts** functioned in Calcutta, Bombay, and Madras.
 
• **Sadar Adalats** were the principal courts of appeal in civil and criminal cases in the provinces.
 
 
 
• **Judicial Reforms under British Rule:**
 
 
• The British introduced several judicial reforms to consolidate their administrative control over India.
 
• The Indian High Courts Act was part of these reforms aimed at improving the efficiency and structure of the judiciary.
 
 
 
• **Indian High Courts Act of 1861:**
 
 
• It allowed the Crown to establish High Courts by Letters Patent in the presidencies.
 
• The High Courts were modeled on the British judicial system, ensuring uniformity and better administration of justice.
 
 
 
• **Modern Relevance:**
 
 
• High Courts continue to function as the principal civil and criminal courts of appeal in India.
 
• The judiciary in India still follows the hierarchical structure introduced during British rule.
